body.x: UniUni (CEO Soo Yeon Han) participated in the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, CES 2024, held in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

UniUni is a company that, under the vision of “providing a service that unites you and me,” has been researching and developing technological solutions to address safety blind spots that threaten vulnerable individuals in society. They have introduced various products and technologies by combining cutting-edge technologies such as IoT and Artificial Intelligence (AI) with universal design. Additionally, leveraging specialized capabilities in deep learning, the company has secured 18 patents, including five registered patents.

UniUni, which received the SMEs and Startups Ministry’s pre-startup package designation and the Top Excellent Company Award before its establishment, has secured approximately 20 certifications and awards. Its accolades include the initial startup package, the Top Excellent Company Award, and the 14th Credit Guarantee Fund’s Startup-NEST program participant. Moreover, UniUni has recently accepted the invitation to participate in the Technology Innovation Program for Startup Growth (TIPS) R&D, earning recognition for its independent technological capabilities and outstanding business viability. Through these achievements, the company is actively exploring opportunities for expansion into domestic and international markets.

At this year’s CES, UniUni unveiled its “Savvy Toilet,” a safety toilet solution - an AIoT smart integrated platform designed for a “safe, secure, and satisfying” restroom experience. The main feature of this platform is the real-time detection of unusual behavior in the restroom using AI technology.

In particular, it utilizes deep learning to identify unauthorized filming, falls, and abnormal behavior within 4 seconds, achieving a high detection accuracy of 99.6%. The system automatically alerts administrators after identifying risks and irregular behavior, enabling prompt responses.

body.cap: A snapshot of the sensor product dedicated to ‘Savvy Toilet’ unveiled by UniUni at the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, CES 2024, held in Las Vegas on the 9th (local time). | Photo - AVING News

body.x: In addition, Savvy Toilet offers various features such as △real-time data collection and an automated refining system for accurate data provision △object detection and mapping of spatial data to identify objects and provide location information △real-time monitoring of customer behavior information presented in dashboard format through the APP service, delivering comprehensive support for safety measures inside the restroom.

The representative from UniUni mentioned, “Visitors of diverse nationalities showed significant interest in our booth, particularly in our sensor and deep learning technologies” and added, “We received numerous intriguing collaboration and business proposals, including specific plans from organizations and companies looking to expand senior care platform business in Europe. Their proposals have opened up possibilities for us to explore entering the global market in the future.”

The UniUni representative further stated, “Participating in CES with a focus on the North American market has brought us various possibilities and opportunities, which makes us pleased,” and continued, “This exhibition has been a catalyst for establishing the direction in which we will advance in the safety and security field based on next-generation technologies, laying the foundation for further growth of the company.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
